purpose: Rules for selecting direct, hierarchy-aware UNI 8290 to IFC occurrence mappings.
acceptance_question: Can an instance of this IFC entity itself honestly receive this UNI code in the context of the full UNI parent path?

selection_gates.rule: The entity must exist in the pinned IFC 4.3.2 entity catalogue.

The entity must be a concrete object occurrence or system eligible for bSDD RelatedIfcEntityNamesList review; abstract, type, relationship, property, context, measure, select, enumeration, function, rule, and resource concepts are excluded.
The meaning must be derived from the complete UNI hierarchy, never from the leaf label alone.
The IFC occurrence itself must perform or embody the UNI function; mere containment, connection, support, fastening, monitoring, or possible participation is insufficient.
Prefer the closest defensible entity or small entity family. Do not add a superclass and all of its descendants merely for coverage.
Avoid deprecated entities when a supported concrete replacement exists; otherwise record the deprecation condition.
Record any required PredefinedType, object property, spatial role, load-bearing role, or system-membership condition that RelatedIfcEntityNamesList cannot express.
A parent mapping is an independent semantic decision and is not the automatic union of child mappings.

1.default_scope: one or a few broad concrete occurrence or system concepts

2.default_scope: a system, functional grouping, assembly, or controlled occurrence family

3.default_scope: an exact occurrence entity or small directly applicable family

selected.meaning: The entity directly represents the UNI technical element or function.
Each selected entity belongs to a small, explicitly bounded family that directly represents the UNI concept.
The entity is directly classifiable only with the recorded distribution-system or functional-system context.
The match is valid only for the recorded IFC PredefinedType value or values.
The match is valid only when a recorded property or role condition is true.
A broad concrete IFC concept is used for a UNI level-1 or level-2 aggregate without inheriting the union of descendants.

rejected.meaning: The name is not an IFC 4.3.2 entity.
The IFC entity represents a type object rather than an occurrence.
The IFC concept is a relationship, property definition, measure, select, enumeration, context, or resource.
The entity may be a component or participant but does not itself carry the UNI function.
The entity may fit the leaf word in another system but not this complete UNI hierarchy path.
The entity is semantically broader than the UNI class and lacks a recordable condition that makes the match reliable.
The entity represents only one optional realization and selecting it would overstate the UNI class.
The deprecated entity is superseded by a supported concrete alternative.
A proxy or generic fallback is unnecessary because a proper entity exists.
The proposal arose only by copying or unioning descendant mappings into a parent.
No defensible direct semantic relationship exists.

screening.meaning: Selected by at least one UNI decision.
Eligible IFC entity was considered but no UNI class directly applies.
Excluded by IFC technical eligibility before semantic comparison.

branch_rules.interpretation: Classify elements by their structural and load-transfer role, not by material, reinforcement, fastening, or possible membership.
conditions: Use load-bearing or structural-role context where an entity can also be non-structural.
Treat reinforcement, tendons, bearings, fasteners, and vibration devices as separate elements only when the UNI leaf directly names their function.

branch_rules.interpretation: Classify exterior horizontal, vertical, and upper enclosure elements by enclosing role and full path; distinguish host construction from dependent finish.
conditions: IfcCovering is valid for a dependent finish or covering, not as a universal enclosure.
Record exterior and orientation context when IFC entity alone does not distinguish it.

branch_rules.interpretation: Classify non-load-bearing internal subdivision, closure, finish, and circulation elements; record internal and non-load-bearing conditions where necessary.
conditions: Do not classify an element here solely because it is physically inside a building.
Distinguish partitions from structural walls using role or property context.

branch_rules.interpretation: Classify external site subdivision, retaining, protection, and access elements according to the complete branch path.
conditions: Do not confuse an exterior building enclosure with an external site partition.
Record retaining, boundary, fence, gate, or access role when required; IFC 4.3.2 has no IfcFence or IfcGate occurrence entity.

branch_rules.interpretation: Read Alimentazione, Macchine, Rete, Terminali, and Allacciamenti through their parent service. Select a distribution system for a system-level unit and media-specific occurrences for technical-element leaves.
conditions: Record the IFC distribution-system PredefinedType or media context.
A generic flow class must not be copied across HVAC, plumbing, gas, electrical, communications, lifting, or waste branches without a direct contextual rationale.
Network branches may include segments and fittings; connection branches require entities that themselves represent the connection, not every connected participant.

branch_rules.interpretation: Distinguish fire, grounding, lightning, and anti-intrusion systems by the parent path; map detection, alarm, protection, and distribution occurrences only to the function they directly perform.
conditions: Use PredefinedType and system context to separate fire, security, earth, and lightning functions.
Do not infer a safety classification merely because equipment may be monitored or protected.

branch_rules.interpretation: Classify fixed or modelled internal equipment by its direct furnishing, functional, or collective equipment role, not merely because it is indoors.
conditions: Exclude loose, unmodelled, or purely spatial inventory concepts.
Service-connected equipment remains in the service branch when its primary UNI function is system delivery.

branch_rules.interpretation: Classify external fixed equipment, landscaping construction, and site circulation surfaces by direct function and placement context.
conditions: Prefer IfcPavement for an external pavement; use IfcCovering only for a dependent finish.
Record external/site context where the IFC entity can also occur internally.

decision_record_requirements.empty_selection_rule: An empty mapping is preferable to a false match and must carry an explicit rationale.
